title: DNeasy PowerSoil Pro for Filters Extractions
author: Maggi Mars
materials: Enter values into designated experiment spreadsheet.
Once thawed, flash centrifuge extraction samples.

steps.title: Set incubator temperature
steps.instruction: Set the mini‑incubator temperature to 65 °C.

steps.title: Gather consumables and reagents
steps.instruction: Collect the following items: Qubit Flex assay tube strips (8‑tube strips, one strip for each standard and one tube per sample; for 16 samples use 2 strips), Qubit 1× dsDNA HS assay working solution (opaque bottle), Qubit 1× dsDNA HS assay standards (box in fridge), a plastic reservoir for multipipetting (in white cardboard box in glass cabinet), a 200 µl 8‑channel multipipettor, a blue 1 ml/1000 µl pipettor, a green pipettor with green tips, a red pipettor, a 200 µl repeater pipettor, sterile dissecting scissors and forceps, 70 % ethanol, ice bucket, petri dishes, and a clean aluminum cold rack.

steps.title: Label and freeze sample tubes
steps.instruction: Label sample tubes with the experiment name and place them in the numbered spaces of the extraction box inside the –80 °C freezer.

steps.title: Clean work surfaces and tools
steps.instruction: Wipe all surfaces, dissecting scissors and forceps with 70 % ethanol before starting.

steps.title: Prepare ice bucket
steps.instruction: Fill the ice bucket with ice and keep it on the bench.

steps.title: Prepare tube layout per sample
steps.instruction: For each sample set out: 1 × PowerSoil Pro bead tube, 1 × MB spin column (do NOT place spin columns in the heated incubator), 3 × 2 ml microcentrifuge tubes, and 1 × 1.5 ml elution tube. Arrange tubes so that you do not reach into the bags; take tubes closest to the bag opening to avoid skin contact.

steps.title: Prepare petri dishes
steps.instruction: Place one sterile petri dish (bottom and lid) for every two samples; use the dish as a workspace for cutting filters.

steps.title: Add CD1 to bead tubes
steps.instruction: Add 800 µl of CD1 to each PowerSoil Pro bead tube that will be used. Return the CD1 bottle to its box.

steps.title: Process each filter sample
steps.instruction: For each sample, perform the substeps below in order.

substeps.instruction: Remove the sample tube from ice; if the filter is frozen solid, let it thaw briefly on ice (only needed for the first few samples).

Using sterile forceps, remove the filter from its tube and cut it into thin strips over a sterile petri dish with clean dissecting scissors. Transfer all filter pieces into the bead tube so they are fully submerged in CD1. Label the bead tube with the sample number from the original tube lid and set the original filter tube aside for later record‑keeping.
Clean the scissors and forceps with 70 % ethanol before handling the next sample; use a fresh petri dish surface for each sample.
Incubate the bead tubes at 65 °C for 10 minutes (do NOT place spin columns in the incubator). While incubating, remove CD3 from storage and label it with the sample numbers.
Transfer the bead tubes to the vortex adapter (white plate with projections) on the Vortex Genie 2, ensuring caps face the centre and tubes click into place. Vortex at high speed for 10 minutes.
Place the bead tubes in a balanced rotor and centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 1 minute at room temperature.

Set the blue 1 ml pipettor to 1000 µl. Press the filter fragments against the tube wall, then aspirate all liquid from the bead tube and dispense into a clean 2 ml microcentrifuge tube bearing the same sample number. Touch the tip to the beads to recover remaining liquid, then discard the bead tube.
Centrifuge the 2 ml tube at 15 000 × g for 1 minute.
Avoid the white film/pellet at the tube bottom; carefully transfer 600 µl of supernatant to a new clean 2 ml tube (same sample label) and discard the previous tube.
Using the green pipettor with green tips, add 200 µl of CD2 to the tube, vortex for ~5 seconds until the mixture becomes white and cloudy, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 1 minute.
Again avoid the white gelatin‑like pellet; transfer 600 µl of supernatant to a new clean 2 ml tube (same sample label) and discard the previous tube.
Give CD3 a gentle swirl (no shaking to avoid foam), add 600 µl of CD3 to the tube, vortex for 5 seconds until homogenised (a density gradient will be visible). Return CD3 to its box.
Pipette 650 µl of the sample (now in CD3) onto the top of the MB spin column (matching sample name). Pipette slowly to avoid bubbles and splash back.
Centrifuge the spin column at 15 000 × g for 1 minute.
Gently remove the spin column from the collection tube, dump the filtrate into waste, then return the spin column to the same collection tube.
Transfer the remaining ~550 µl of sample (keep pipette set to 650 µl) to the top of the spin column. Discard the previous microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the spin column again at 15 000 × g for 1 minute.
Move the spin column to a new clean 2 ml collection tube (no caps).
Add 500 µl of solution EA to the top of the spin column, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 1 minute.

Discard the flow‑through by removing the spin column from the collection tube and emptying the tube into waste; place the spin column back into the same collection tube (avoid touching the column sides).
Dry the spin column by centrifuging at 16 000 g for 2 minutes (collection tubes will appear mostly empty).
Add 500 µl of CD5 to the top of the spin column, return CD5 to its box, and centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer the spin column to a new clean 2 ml collection tube, then move it into a 1.5 ml elution tube (caps stay open).

Using the green pipettor with green tips, pipette 50 µl of CD6 directly onto the centre of the white silicate region of the spin column (do NOT touch the filter or the plastic rim). Return CD6 to its box.
Place the spin column‑elution tube assembly in a centrifuge rack with elution‑tube caps pointing inward and centrifuge at 15 000 g for 1 minute.

Remove the spin column, close the elution‑tube caps, discard the spin column, and place the elution tube on an aluminum cold rack. Keep the rack on ice or in the fridge (cold racks are stored in the fridge; if ice melts, drain water and refill). This is a good break point; samples may remain on ice or in the fridge for up to one hour.

steps.title: Wear gloves and decontaminate
steps.instruction: Wear gloves for all molecular work. Frequently clean gloved hands with 70 % ethanol, especially after touching any surface not already on the molecular bench (e.g., hair, face, clothing). Use filtered pipette tips for all steps.

steps.title: Prepare Qubit working solution
steps.instruction: Calculate the volume of working solution needed: (number of standards + number of samples) × 200 µl + 100 µl. Use the blue 1 ml pipettor to transfer the calculated volume into the plastic reservoir, dispensing 1 ml aliquots as needed.

steps.title: Dispense working solution to assay tubes
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µl 8‑channel pipettor, add 190 µl of working solution to each standard tube and 195 µl to each sample tube. Re‑use tips only if they are clean (green tips). If no standards are being run, skip to step 13.

steps.title: Add standards (if used)
steps.instruction: If running standards, use a 200 µl repeater pipettor to add 10 µl of standard 1 to all eight standard 1 tubes and 10 µl of standard 2 to all eight standard 2 tubes. Touch the pipette tip to the working‑solution reservoir before aspirating to ensure the standard leaves the tip (surface tension). Change tips between standards (green tips).

steps.title: Add sample aliquots for Qubit
steps.instruction: Using a red pipettor, add 5 µl of each DNA sample to its corresponding sample tube. Perform samples in order and label the start and end numbers on the strip tab.

steps.title: Mix and incubate Qubit tubes
steps.instruction: Vortex all assay strips briefly, then incubate in the dark for 2 minutes. If standards were used, return the standard tubes to the fridge after incubation.

steps.title: Run Qubit assay
steps.instruction: Open the 1× dsDNA HS assay program on the Qubit instrument. Select whether standards are being run (check the date of the last run). Load the standard strips first (if applicable) and run them, then load the sample strips and run them. Ensure the correct number of tubes is selected, there are no bubbles, and the units are set to ng/µl with a sample volume of 5 µl. Record all values.

steps.title: Clean up after Qubit
steps.instruction: Empty the ice bucket and let it dry. Return all kits to their storage locations and wipe the bench with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Retrieve and thaw PCR reagents
steps.instruction: Take out forward and reverse 16S Illumina primers, KAPA HiFi HotStart polymerase, PCR tube strips, a 1.5 ml DNA LoBind tube (labelled MM), and the extracted DNA samples from the –80 °C freezer. Allow all reagents to thaw.

steps.title: Prepare Master Mix
steps.instruction: In the 1.5 ml LoBind tube, combine for each sample (plus one extra for a control): 1 µl forward primer, 1 µl reverse primer, and 12.5 µl KAPA HiFi HotStart. Mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Dispense Master Mix to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µl repeater pipettor, add 14.5 µl of the Master Mix to each PCR tube.

steps.title: Add DNA template to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Pipette 10.5 µl of each extracted DNA sample into the corresponding PCR tube using a grey VWR pipettor with red tips. Mix the sample and Master Mix by pipetting, changing the tip after each sample.

steps.title: Seal and spin PCR plates
steps.instruction: Secure the lids of all PCR tubes. If processing 32 samples, apply a 32‑well adhesive seal on top. Quick‑spin the plate in a centrifuge to collect liquid at the bottom of each tube.

steps.title: Run thermal cycler program
steps.instruction: Open the thermal cycler, load the blue rack, and centre the PCR plate (balance with empty strips on either side if needed). Select ‘Setup Run’, choose the open method, and pick the protocol named ‘kapa hifi 16s’. Verify that the program shows a 25 µl reaction volume with the correct stage durations and temperatures. Click ‘Next’ and start the run. Monitor the screen until the program reaches ‘Stage 2’ to confirm it is running correctly.

steps.title: Final cleaning and storage
steps.instruction: Clean all surfaces with 70 % ethanol. Return the extracted DNA samples to the –80 °C freezer, and place KAPA HiFi HotStart polymerase and Illumina primers back in their designated bags/boxes in the –20 °C freezer.
